entries.description: Register.

**Ship the four subcommands** against the existing `docs/modules.yaml` contract — read the shape `moduleAuthoring.ts` writes today and match it; this is a port, and a format change here would strand every repo that already has a manifest.

**Make the dangerous paths refuse.** `delete` and `rename` must refuse a module with a **running session**, and must route any `session-state.json` mutation through the sanctioned writer rather than touching the file. This is the invariant the set exists to restore.

**Rollback on partial failure.** A create that scaffolds a directory and then fails to append the manifest entry must leave neither behind. Ship a falsifier that injects the failure and asserts nothing is stranded — `L-112-1`: a gate that only ever passes proves nothing.
**Cross-provider verification.**
**Required portion of the full test suite.**
**Close-out.**

Register.

**Point the five existing context-menu commands at the CLI**, passing an explicit repo root and slug, showing output and refreshing the tree (verdict §4). **Invoke the resolved workspace-venv interpreter, never a bare `python`** — the launcher must run the same interpreter the install flow targets (`venvPython(...)` / the `dabblerSessionSets.pythonPath` setting), because a bare `python` on `PATH` is the documented cause of the `No module named ai_router` mis-diagnosis (`describeAiRouterImportFailure`, and the constitution's own warning). Branch on the CLI's exit codes: `3` = refused, nothing written; `4` = write failure. Then **delete the lifecycle logic from `moduleAuthoring.ts`** rather than leaving two implementations — the duplication is the defect Set 120 spent a session removing elsewhere. **This reaches `gitScaffold.ts` whether or not it is named here:** `scaffoldDefaultModuleAndLifecycleSets` calls `scaffoldNewModule`, so the default-module scaffold becomes Python-backed in this session. **Do not change any command id:** renaming one breaks keybindings, `when`-clauses and Layer 3 fixtures, and the 2026-08-11 menu trim deliberately renamed titles only, verified against all 52 ids. Fold in residual **`S122-S1-R1`** while here (Session 1's `disposition.json`): `_existing_lifecycle_slug` matches a module's lifecycle sets by basename suffix, so creating module `api` reuses `payment-api`'s sets; the identity test should be that the name, minus its numeric prefix, equals `<slug>-<kind>` exactly.

**Echo the command before running it** (operator, 2026-08-11: *"echoed... so developers know what commands are being executed"*). Show the exact `python -m ai_router.modules …` line the extension is about to run, in a surface the developer can read and copy, then run it with deterministic code per standing decision 2. A developer who wants to run it by hand should be able to copy what they just saw and get the same result.

**Fix `src/utils/cancelLifecycle.ts:296`** — it calls `atomicWriteFile(statePath, JSON.stringify(state, null, 2) + "\n")`, so **TypeScript writes `session-state.json` today**, reached via `deleteModule`. Verified still present 2026-08-11. It is the concrete violation that justified this whole set. Also put **`copyModuleDecompositionPrompt` on the context menu**; it works and is palette-only, and it is the operator's *"copy-prompt context menu items for modules"* one manifest entry away. Use the `Copy X` label convention, no colon.
**Cross-provider verification.**

**Required portion of the full test suite.** `package.json` is the extension MANIFEST, so **`L-064-12` applies**: the full `npm run test:playwright` is owed here alongside pytest, run after the last edit and never before.
**Close-out.**
Wiring the five module commands to the Python CLI: surveyed the TypeScript surface, folded in residual S122-S1-R1 (exact-identity lifecycle-set match, mutation-checked falsifier).

Every router CLI run echoes the exact, copy-pasteable command line to the shared 'Dabbler Commands' output channel BEFORE spawning, then the output. One builder feeds both the echoed line and the spawned argv, so what the developer sees and what runs cannot disagree.

Removed the TypeScript session-state.json writer entirely (operator decision, journaled): added a cancel/restore CLI to ai_router/session_lifecycle.py, routed cancelLifecycleCommands.ts through it, trimmed cancelLifecycle.ts to readers (549 -> 142 lines). copyModuleDecompositionPrompt added to the module context menu. Also shipped the operator-directed start_session register-tick fix.

Cross-provider verification (gpt-5.5; anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider). Discovery round 1 fanned out 2/2 and returned two blocking Majors, both against the command-echo promise: a '> ' prompt glyph welded onto the only visible command line, and PowerShell quoting that would not run (a leading quoted exe needs '&', and '\"' is not a PowerShell escape). Supplementary round 2 found nothing new. Both remediated once, with falsifiers; remediation-review round 3 returned VERIFIED, 2 accepted / 0 rejected. Artifacts: s2-conventions.md, s2-verification*.md, s2-issues.json, s2-remediation-round-1.md.

Full pytest of record after the last code change: 4213 passed, 9 skipped in 906s. Layer 2 (npm run test:unit): 1421 passing, 2 pending. Full npm run test:playwright owed here because package.json is the extension MANIFEST (L-064-12): 20 passed / 11 failed. Eight of the eleven pass in isolation (parallel-load flake on a 4-vCPU box, confirmed spec by spec, and icon-render-mechanism additionally confirmed green at HEAD and green again after a recompile). Two were the deliberate register-tick behaviour change in work-explorer-steps.spec.ts and are updated and green. One is KNOWN-RED and operator-attested: vsix-first-run-walkthrough.spec.ts does a real network pip install, which fetches dabbler-ai-router 0.34.0 from PyPI -- a wheel that predates ai_router.modules -- so the now-Python-backed default-module scaffold cannot run on a true cold start. That is the exact regression Session 4 exists to prevent; it owns the fix and is the release gate, so neither registry publishes while it is red. All three runs recorded via run_of_record.
Register.

**Declare the floor, and make the install satisfy it.** Define the minimum router the extension requires (`dabbler-ai-router>=1.0.0` if `ai_router.modules` ships in the staged `1.0.0`) in ONE place both the install path and the precondition read — two independently-maintained version constants is the drift defect this repo keeps re-finding (L-069-1). The setup install must **upgrade an existing older installation** rather than accept it: today only `mode: "update"` passes `--upgrade` (`aiRouterInstall.ts:431`), and `mode: "install"` does not. Prefer widening the existing install path over adding a third mode.

**Probe the capability, and refuse to proceed without it.** After installing, probe **the same venv interpreter the launcher will use** by importing `ai_router.modules` — never infer success from pip's exit code alone (L-125-1: compare what the transport CAN DO, not what it returns; L-079-3: provisioning is exactly where silent fail-open paths hide). On failure, do **not** run Python-backed default-module creation; report it and leave a supported retry path — `describeAiRouterImportFailure` is already the right message and the Copilot-seat gate (`skip-install-incomplete`, `gitScaffold.ts:638`) is already the right pattern. Then **fix retryability**: `gitScaffold.ts:530` gates default-module creation on the manifest having been created *in that call*, so a second setup attempt after a failed install can never produce the default module — the user's only recovery is deleting a `docs/modules.yaml` nobody told them about. Gate on the module being absent, not on who created the manifest.

**Dogfood the true cold start, and the upgrade.** L-079-3 is binding for any set shipping provisioning: at least one walk must begin from a **fresh empty folder** with no pre-seeded config and assert the provisioned artifacts exist. Two scenarios, both automated — the set declares `requiresUAT: false` and that flag is immutable, so this is a scripted/Layer 3 dogfood, **not** an operator walk: (a) a clean project with no `.venv` finishes setup with `ai_router.modules` importable from the created venv and the default module present; (b) a project whose `.venv` holds `dabbler-ai-router==0.34.0` is upgraded to a compatible release by setup. Assert the failure path too: an unavailable install attempts no Python-backed module mutation, and re-running setup after that failure succeeds **without** deleting the already-created `docs/modules.yaml`.
**Cross-provider verification.**

**Required portion of the full test suite.** This session touches the scaffold and install surfaces the Explorer renders from; if it edits `package.json`, **`L-064-12` applies** and the full `npm run test:playwright` is owed alongside pytest, run after the last edit and never before.
**Close-out.**
Registered session 3 (github-copilot / claude-opus-5, high).
Declaring the router version floor in one place and widening the install path to upgrade an existing older installation.

MINIMUM_ROUTER_VERSION + PYPI_REQUIREMENT declared once in aiRouterInstall.ts; the install requirement and the capability precondition both derive from it (L-069-1), pinned by a test that fails if either is hard-coded. mode:install now passes --upgrade, so an existing older venv is upgraded rather than reported already-satisfied.

probeRouterCapability imports ai_router.modules with the VENV interpreter the launcher uses (L-125-1), never inferring success from pip exit codes; a failed probe flips the install outcome to ok:false with no fail-open branch. gitScaffold gates default-module creation on decideDefaultModuleScaffold (module ABSENT, not manifest provenance), which fixes retryability: a retry after a failed install now scaffolds without deleting docs/modules.yaml.
Authoring the cold-start and upgrade dogfoods (L-079-3).

New lane npm run test:dogfood (src/test/dogfood/), 4 scenarios, real venv + real network pip, no seams: (a) clean project with no .venv finishes setup with ai_router.modules importable and the scaffold gate saying scaffold; (b) a venv holding a REAL dabbler-ai-router==0.34.0 from PyPI is upgraded past the floor, with the vacuity premise asserted first (0.34.0 must NOT provide ai_router.modules); (c) an unresolvable install attempts no Python-backed mutation and a re-run recovers with docs/modules.yaml untouched; (d) the probe answers for the venv it is given, not the host. Caught a real defect while authoring: passing a venv-shaped pythonPath made ensureVenv provision into the REPO venv, so the cold-start scenario had been passing vacuously (13s vs 38s). Fixed by resolving sys.base_prefix and asserting the venv lands under the temp project.
Running the phased cross-provider verification loop.

Cross-provider verification (gpt-5.5; anthropic excluded as the orchestrator effective provider). Discovery round 1 fanned out 2/2 and returned 4 blocking Majors reducing to 2 classes: the capability probe answered for the install venv rather than the interpreter the launchers resolve, and the dogfood asserted the GATE instead of the outcome. Supplementary round 2 added 1 more: the new CI lane depended on untracked local Python state. Remediation-review round 3 accepted 1 and REJECTED 2, catching a regression the round-1 fix introduced (the launcher interpreter was resolved eagerly, before .venv existed, which would have made the ordinary cold start report a good install as failed). Fixed by making it a thunk resolved after install, plus a mutation-checked falsifier. Round 4: VERIFIED, 5 accepted / 0 rejected, 0 findings.
Running the full suites owed by covers: pytest (Layer 1) and full Playwright (Layer 3, owed because package.json is the extension MANIFEST - L-064-12), after the last code change.

All three layers run after the last code change and recorded via run_of_record. Layer 1 pytest: 4214 passed, 9 skipped in 662s (digest 1a94cea85bbf). Layer 2 mocha: 1450 passing, 2 pending in 63s (digest f440dafe1fe1). Layer 3 Playwright FULL, owed because package.json is the extension MANIFEST (L-064-12): 31/31 passed in 6.7m at 2 workers, the count CI uses per residual S122-S2-R2 - including vsix-first-run-walkthrough, which Session 2 closed out as KNOWN-RED. The first pytest attempt failed one test: the anti-resurrection guard scanned build/lib, a pip-generated copy of its own source. Fixed by excluding build/ and .eggs from the shared scan with a narrow falsifier; classified A4.2 by post_round_delta and settled by a delta-scoped remediation-review (round 5, VERIFIED).
